title: Significant ordinary Nernst effect contribution to spin-orbit torque harmonic Hall measurements in metallic structures
authors: Igor Lyalin, C. C. Chiang, C. L. Chien
abstract: The harmonic Hall measurements are commonly used to quantify the spin-orbit torque in ferromagnet/normal metal bilayers. The contribution from ordinary Nernst effect to the second harmonic voltages is usually assumed to be negligible and omitted in the data analysis. We show that in Cr/Co bilayers the ordinary Nernst effect cannot be neglected and can lead to largely exaggerated values of spin-orbit torque efficiency. Conducting additional experiments, we estimate the Nernst coefficient of Cr and find it comparable to the values reported for other metals. Consequently, the ordinary Nernst effect should be carefully considered when employing the harmonic Hall technique to quantify spin-orbit torque in metals, while the results of some previous works might need to be re-examined.
summary: This work investigates how the ordinary Nernst effect contaminates measurements designed to quantify spin-orbit torque using Harmonic Hall techniques on metallic bilayers. The authors demonstrate that neglecting this thermal contribution leads to significantly exaggerated SOT values, necessitating careful re-analysis of existing literature.
main_problem: The ordinary Nernst effect (ONE) contribution to second harmonic voltages in Harmonic Hall measurements is significant and often neglected, leading to overestimation of spin-orbit torque (SOT) efficiency.
main_result: The ONE cannot be ignored when quantifying SOT in metallic bilayers; correcting for it significantly reduces the calculated SOT efficiency values, suggesting previous results may need re-examination.
method: Harmonic Hall measurements are performed on FM/NM bilayers using sinusoidal currents, and the measured signal is analyzed by fitting models that explicitly include the ONE contribution alongside standard SOT terms.
model_or_system:
The study focuses on metallic structures like Cr/Co bilayers ($	ext{sub}/	ext{Co}/	ext{Cr}$ and $	ext{sub}/	ext{Cr}/	ext{Co}$). The analysis involves separating contributions from Damping-like SOT, Field-like SOT, thermal effects (related to temperature gradients $
abla T$), and the ONE.
key_observables: Second harmonic Hall resistance ($R_{2\omega}^{xy}$), Damping-like SOT efficiency ($\xi^E_{	ext{DL}}$), and the Ordinary Nernst coefficient ($N$).
important_parameters: Stacking order of FM/NM layers, magnetic field dependence, and temperature gradient magnitude.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling thermal artifacts using simulations (e.g., COMSOL) and assuming that the ONE contribution can be isolated or estimated from reference samples.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of HH measurement geometry and show the angular dependence of $R_{2\omega}^{xy}$ for different bilayer stacks, highlighting large thermal backgrounds.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the measured second harmonic voltage by comparing results from standard SOT models against advanced models that incorporate the ONE and thermal effects, leading to corrected quantitative estimates for $\xi^E_{	ext{DL}}$.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous separation of multiple competing physical mechanisms (SOT vs. Nernst/Thermal) mirrors challenges in isolating fundamental quantum responses in complex mesoscopic systems.
